title: Heat Pump vs Furnace: Costs, Efficiency, Comfort, and Climate Fit - PICKHVAC
channel: How to Choose Best HVAC Systems
summary: A 2025 HVAC buyer's guide comparing heat pumps and gas furnaces on efficiency, cost, cold-weather performance and incentives, with a break-even price formula.

assertions.quote: Because it moves heat, it can deliver two to four units of heat energy per unit of electricity.
Many can operate down to -5°F to -13°F, maintaining a significant share of their rated capacity at 5°F.
“Heat pumps do not work below freezing.” Modern cold-climate models heat effectively well below 32°F, many to -13°F.
Operating cost depends on local electricity and gas prices, climate, equipment efficiency, and thermostat settings.
If local electricity is lower, the heat pump is cheaper to run; if higher, the furnace wins.
Electric resistance heat is costly; heat pumps are 2–4× more efficient than resistance heat.
AC + Furnace (Full HVAC) $9,000–$18,000 Comparable to a single heat pump system covering both modes.
If the AC is near end-of-life, a heat pump can replace both systems at once
This approach optimizes operating cost and comfort in cold climates without sacrificing AC efficiency.
In freezing weather, outdoor coils accumulate frost. Heat pumps periodically reverse to melt frost, briefly pausing heating.
Homes with 100A service may need upgrades, though smart panels and load-shedding devices can sometimes avoid a full service replacement.
Qualifying electric heat pumps may receive up to $2,000 per year in federal tax credits.
Income-based electrification rebates authorized by federal law are rolling out state by state
